_notes: The rubric and the category targets were written before any adapter scores exist.
Documents are referenced, not bundled: a URL plus a SHA-256. Copyrighted PDFs
(textbooks, journals) are never added to a downloadable corpus; the two already
in inputs/ stay local and are marked as not redistributable.
`sha256: null` means the document has not been fetched and pinned yet. fetch.py
reports those as unpinned and refuses to score them until --record pins the hash.
JSON rather than YAML so that fetch.py, the tests and CI need no new dependency;
the schema and the rules for adding a document are in bench/README.md.

coverage._target: 6 documents per category before results are published

single-column.stresses: plain reading order; baseline for every other category

two-column.stresses: XY-cut column separation, running heads between columns

textbook.stresses: TOC, index, glossary, figure captions, per-chapter summaries

tables.stresses: financial tables and 10-K layouts; where every extractor loses data

slides.stresses: sparse pages, large type, no paragraphs, one line per bullet

non-latin.stresses: the unicode-aware filter and the English-only stop markers

scanned.stresses: no-text-layer detection, OCR availability, honest skipping

documents.license: Springer, all rights reserved; present in this repo as a development sample
documents.why: front matter with a real TOC, an index and a glossary: the document that broke the percent trim

documents.license: IJRTE, all rights reserved; present in this repo as a development sample
documents.why: two columns with repeating journal furniture; short enough that a percentage trim is catastrophic
dense single-column body with many figures and equations
long appendix and a references section that must truncate cleanly
table-heavy results section: the category where extractors diverge most
75 pages: the runtime and memory case, not just the quality case
